stories.headline: Jets fall 23–12 at Chicago as Bears hold the ball for nearly 43 minutes
stories.summary: The Jets fell behind early and lost 23–12 to the Bears at Soldier Field on Sunday, dropping to 1–3 while Chicago improved to 3–1. Kyle Monangai ran for two Bears touchdowns, and Chicago piled up 492 total yards and 34 first downs while holding the ball for 42:45; the Jets went 0-for-7 on third down. Minkah Fitzpatrick, in his first action since Week 1, had 16 tackles and the team’s first interception of the season, but the Jets were flagged 12 times, including three penalties that wiped out other interceptions. Geno Smith’s 58-yard touchdown to Isaiah Williams came late, and head coach Aaron Glenn said he was “very, very disappointed on a number of different levels.”

stories.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro leads Lula in Brazil’s early count, just above the line that avoids a runoff
stories.summary: Brazil’s electoral court showed Flávio Bolsonaro, the conservative senator and son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, ahead of President Lula in Sunday’s first-round count. At 5:32 PM Eastern, with about 37% of polling stations counted, Flávio had 50.63% of valid votes to Lula’s 41.23%, a gap of about 4 million votes. A candidate needs more than half of the valid votes in the final count to win outright; otherwise the top two meet in a runoff on October 25. The count was far from finished, and several northeastern states where Lula leads were less than a third counted, so the shares were expected to move. The final Datafolha poll had shown Lula slightly ahead.

stories.headline: U.S. pulls all its bombers out of RAF Fairford after last month’s terror-plot arrests
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force has sent every bomber it had deployed at RAF Fairford in England back to home stations in the United States, a Pentagon spokesperson confirmed to CBS News on Sunday. The move follows a security incident last month in which five British men in their 20s were arrested near the base, which American bombers have used for strikes on Iran; police found gasoline in three vans tied to the suspects but no explosives. A dual U.K.-Iranian national was later arrested on suspicion of plotting an attack and has been released on bail. The Pentagon said B-1, B-2 and B-52 crews remain ready to strike “anywhere, anytime,” including from the continental United States.

stories.headline: Arizona appeals court tosses a killer’s sentence because the judge ‘loved’ an AI video of the victim
stories.summary: The Arizona Court of Appeals has ordered a new sentencing for Gabriel Paul Horcasitas, who got the maximum 10½ years for the 2021 road-rage shooting death of Christopher Pelkey. At the 2025 hearing, Pelkey’s sister played an AI-generated video in which a replica of Pelkey offered “forgiveness,” and Maricopa County Judge Todd Lang said, “I loved that AI.” The appeals judges wrote that the video “clearly impacted the sentencing judge” and “does not reflect actual events,” making the sentencing “fundamentally unfair.” The manslaughter sentence was vacated and sent back for resentencing.

stories.headline: North Korea’s new missile test could put Guam in range as Kim brushes off Trump
stories.summary: North Korea fired what it called an intermediate-range strategic missile on October 3, part of a “hypersonic strategic weapon system” that state media said flew about 621 miles into waters off the east coast, with Kim Jong Un watching. Former U.S. Forces Korea analyst Sydney Seiler told Fox News Digital that a missile in that class, which flies roughly 3,000 to 5,000 kilometers, would bring Guam, parts of Alaska and Japan into range. Hours after the launch, Trump told an Ohio rally, “I get along great with Kim Jong Un.” Seiler said the test likely was not a direct answer to Trump, but “North Korea simply isn’t interested in talking right now.”

stories.headline: Trump renews his $5,000 check promise, but only if Republicans keep Congress
stories.summary: In a Truth Social video on Saturday, Trump said that if Republicans win the House and Senate in November, he will give every adult citizen $5,000. He has not said where the money would come from or who would approve it; CNBC estimates the cost at roughly $1.2 trillion, which would need an act of Congress. The pledge comes alongside $90 payments to 20.8 million Medicare enrollees and $500 Obamacare “refund” checks already going out. Rep. David Schweikert, R-Ariz., has vowed to fight the idea over deficit and interest-rate worries, and polls are split: Rasmussen found likely voters 47% to 48% on it, while 57% in an Economist/YouGov survey doubted he would deliver.

stories.headline: Sen. John Kennedy says he is thinking about a 2028 run if ‘a bunch of goobers’ jump in
stories.summary: Asked on NBC’s “Meet the Press” on Sunday whether he is thinking about running for president, Louisiana Republican Sen. John Kennedy answered, “Yeah.” He said his plan for now is to seek re-election to the Senate in 2028, but “if a bunch of goobers run, and I think they’re goobers and one of the goobers might win, and I think I could do a better job, I would consider running.” Kennedy would not say why voters should pick him over Vice President JD Vance, who is widely seen as a likely candidate, and said a full field would be good for both parties.

stories.headline: Utah’s colleges approve security upgrades a year after Charlie Kirk’s assassination
stories.summary: The Utah System of Higher Education on Friday approved a campus security review prompted by Charlie Kirk’s killing during a live debate event at Utah Valley University a little more than a year ago. The report lists 25 areas for improvement across the state’s campuses, including a standard process for securing campus events, real-time sharing of threat information between schools, and better communication with police and private security working events. Keith Squires, the state Department of Public Safety chief and one of the authors, called it a chance to bring every campus up to the same level of safety. Tyler Robinson, who is accused of killing Kirk, has pleaded not guilty.

stories.headline: DHS tells Paramore’s Hayley Williams to thank ICE officers after her ‘F— ICE’ concert outburst
stories.summary: Paramore frontwoman Hayley Williams shouted “F— ICE!” and “Free Palestine!” during her solo show Saturday night in Chula Vista, California, while performing her song “Ice in My OJ,” lines she has been adding throughout her 2026 tour. A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson answered on Sunday: “America is grateful all the time for our federal law enforcement officers who keep us safe. We suggest Ms. Williams to thank them for their service, not belittle their sacrifice.” DHS says it recorded 647 assaults on ICE personnel between January 2025 and September 2026, compared with 37 in the comparable 2021–2022 period.

stories.headline: Florida TikTok ‘grey hat hacker’ is jailed again over posts exposing women’s private data
stories.summary: Mark Stephen Asea, 36, of Port St. Lucie, a TikTok creator who calls himself a “demonologist” and “Grey Hat Hacker,” was booked into the St. Lucie County Jail on September 30 on a felony charge of offense against computer users, with bond set at $35,000. Two women told police their private information showed up in his posts; in one video he allegedly taunted a woman with “let’s talk about your actual password” and her last 10 online purchases. Asea was first arrested in April on stalking and computer charges, which prosecutors dropped in May before filing the new computer-access charge in September.

stories.headline: Apple CEO John Ternus is working hands-on in the design studio several times a week
stories.summary: About a month into the job, Apple CEO John Ternus has immersed himself in the company’s industrial design and human interface teams, working in the studio several times a week and sometimes more than once a day, according to Mark Gurman’s reporting summarized by 9to5Mac. Former CEO Tim Cook reportedly visited about once a month. Ternus has also focused on refilling design roles after departures to Meta and OpenAI, promoting junior designers and hiring from outside. Apple is not searching for a Jony Ive-style chief design officer; Molly Anderson and Steve Lemay lead the two teams, with Ternus making the final design calls.

stories.headline: Mac malware hides its commands inside a public iCloud calendar event
stories.summary: Kaspersky researchers found a new version of MacSync, an information-stealing malware for macOS, that in one infection chain pulled hidden commands from the description of a public iCloud calendar event and fed them to the Mac’s command shell to download more malware. The calendar does not infect anyone by itself; the attack starts after a user runs a malicious app, often disguised as free or cracked software or delivered through fake “copy and run this command” prompts. The new version also disguises itself as Finder to survive restarts, and attackers promoted a fake crypto wallet called Toria on X and Telegram.

stories.headline: ‘The Book of Elon’ author says Musk is driven by curiosity and mission more than money
stories.summary: Eric Jorgenson, author of “The Book of Elon: A Guide to Purpose and Success,” told Fox News Digital that he reviewed millions of words of Musk’s interviews and appearances to pull out the ideas behind Tesla, SpaceX and xAI. He says Musk’s work flows from what Musk calls a “philosophy of curiosity,” and that his ideas about multi-planetary life and electric and self-driving cars date back to his college years. The book walks through Musk’s five-step engineering process, known as “the algorithm,” and how his companies use it. Jorgenson says his goal is to “create one million Musks” by teaching readers the methods.

stories.headline: Devin Townsend opens up about a 36-year breakup and the money crunch that sent him back on tour
stories.summary: Former Strapping Young Lad frontman Devin Townsend told the Sixty Scales And The Truth podcast that a “financial Armageddon” pushed him back on stage a year and a half after announcing an indefinite break from touring. He is in the middle of “Metamorphosis,” a 23-show solo tour across 10 European countries. Townsend said his dog died and he split with his partner of 36 years, calling it “devastating,” and said he does not plan to go home to British Columbia and expects to relocate to Spain. His orchestral album “The Moth” came out in May.

stories.headline: Trumbull boys soccer wins its third straight, edging New Canaan 1–0; Wilton is next Tuesday
stories.summary: Trumbull’s defense carried the Eagles past New Canaan 1–0 on Friday, their third win in a row, raising their record to 8–3–1. Trumbull hosts Wilton at 6:00 p.m. on Tuesday. The Warriors, ranked 40th in MaxPreps’ Connecticut rankings, are 6–3–2 after a surprise 3–2 loss to 170th-ranked Ludlowe on Friday and have gone 2–3–2 since a four-game winning streak ended.
